title: Evaluating safeguarding in multi-turn conversations with AI assistants
abstract: arXiv:2611.26009v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conversational AI assistants are now used for personal and emotional support. Developers report improvements in how new models respond to sensitive conversations, yet users and civil society continue to raise concerns about their behaviour in real-world, repeated interactions that safety evaluations rarely capture. Often, evaluations present signs of distress clearly and in a single message, even though people may reveal their struggles gradually in otherwise ordinary conversations. We worked with three community mental health support workers to test if models provide the same level of safeguarding when cues are shared all at once or gradually over time. We designed nine scenarios in which a user shares cues related to depression, psychosis, or domestic abuse. translated_title: 评估AI助手多轮对话中的安全保障机制
translated_abstract: 会话式AI助手如今被广泛用于个人和情感支持。开发者报告称新模型在应对敏感对话方面有所改进，但用户和公民社会仍然对模型在真实世界中反复交互时的行为表示担忧，而这类场景往往被现有安全评估所忽略。通常，评估中痛苦信号会清晰地在单条消息中呈现，然而现实中人们往往是在看似平常的对话中逐渐流露出自己的困境。我们与三名社区心理健康支持工作者合作，测试模型在信号一次性全部给出或随时间逐渐给出时，能否提供同等水平的安全保障。我们设计了九个场景，用户在其中分享与抑郁、精神障碍或家庭虐待相关的线索。针对每个场景，支持工作者确立了黄金标准回应，范围从引导用户获取支持资源，到暂停日常任务以处理安全保障问题。我们向五……（摘要截断）
tldr: 该论文与社区心理健康支持工作者合作设计了九个多轮对话场景，发现AI助手在痛苦线索逐渐显现的日常对话中可能无法保持与信号一次性明确呈现时同等的安全保障水平，从而揭示了现有安全评估方法的不足。
en_tdlr: Collaborating with community mental health support workers across nine multi-turn scenarios, this paper shows that AI assistants may provide weaker safeguarding when distress cues emerge gradually in conversation than when presented clearly in a single message, exposing a gap in current safety evaluations.
